/article-technical-seo.html.main_text: Home/Learning librarylesson / MBK GLOBALTechnical SEO for a Small Portfolio WebsiteSearch visibility starts with pages that are accessible, understandable and worth finding.IN THIS GUIDEProject overviewBakhtawar KhanFounder, MBK Global2 min read · Practical learning notesLearn. Apply. Make it your own.More learning resources ↗MBK JOURNAL / SEO / DISCOVERY← All articlesNEW SEO / DISCOVERYPRACTICAL NOTES / BAKHTAWAR KHANGive each important page a descriptive title, a concise page-specific meta description and a clear main heading. Use meaningful internal links so people and crawlers can discover projects, services, articles and contact details without relying only on interactive controls.Check that the canonical URL matches the preferred public URL, that the sitemap contains real canonical pages and that robots rules do not block important content. Inspect the rendered page, response status and indexability in Search Console. A sitemap helps discovery; it does not guarantee indexing or rankings.Write articles that answer a real question and include your own explanation, examples, limitations and sources when relevant. Avoid creating dozens of near-identical keyword pages or stuffing meta keywords. Keep images compressed and give meaningful images useful alt text.After publishing, inspect important URLs, fix broken links and monitor Search Console for indexing issues. Rankings depend on competition, content quality, links, user intent and many other factors, so avoid guarantees.Further reading: Official documentation ↗BAKHTAWAR KHAN · SEO / DISCOVERYDiscuss a related project ↗Back to the MBK journal ↗

/web-performance-and-ux-guide.html.main_text: Home/Web Performance and User Experience Guidelesson / MBK GLOBALWeb Performance and User Experience GuidePerformance is part of usability: pages should show meaningful content quickly, remain stable as they load, and respond reliably to keyboard, touch and pointer input.IN THIS GUIDE01Prioritize what appears first02Size images deliberately03Reduce font-loading delays04Test responsive behavior05Measure rather than assumeBakhtawar KhanFounder, MBK Global2 min read · Practical learning notesLearn. Apply. Make it your own.More learning resources ↗MBK Global · Practical guidePrioritize what appears firstIdentify the primary above-the-fold content and avoid lazy-loading the main visual when it is needed for the initial experience. Use fetch priority only for a genuinely important image and do not preload every asset.Size images deliberatelySet width and height attributes when dimensions are known so the browser can reserve space. Use responsive image sizes where practical, preserve aspect ratio, and lazy-load suitable below-the-fold images. Do not rehost third-party images without permission.Reduce font-loading delaysAvoid CSS @import chains for web fonts. Use explicit stylesheet links and preconnect only to origins actually needed. Provide a sensible fallback stack and use font-display: swap when self-hosting or configuring fonts.Test responsive behaviorCheck representative narrow mobile widths, tablet and desktop layouts. Look for horizontal overflow, clipped navigation, unreadable text, tap targets that are too small and forms that are hard to complete.Measure rather than assumeCore Web Vitals goals are LCP at or below 2.5 seconds, INP at or below 200 milliseconds and CLS at or below 0.1. These are targets, not results; distinguish local lab tests from real-user field data and retest after deployment. About this guide: This is general educational guidance. Adapt recommendations to your site's actual stack, risk and audience, and verify changes before publishing. Explore related work: web development, projects, and contact.

/ai-chatbots-explained.html.main_text: Home/AI Chatbots Explained: How They Work and Where They Are UsefulField guide / BAKHTAWAR KHANAI Chatbots Explained: How They Work and Where They Are UsefulA practical guide to conversational models, approved knowledge, tool integrations and the limits of automated answers.Explore the work ↗Start a conversation ↗Educational guide · By Bakhtawar Khan · General guidance, not a claim of personally tested provider integrations.01 / FIELD NOTESWhat an AI chatbot actually doesAn AI chatbot produces a response from the conversation and the information supplied to a model. Unlike a fixed menu, it can interpret different phrasings and generate a natural-language answer. That flexibility is useful, but it is not evidence that every answer is correct. A system can sound confident while misunderstanding a question or inventing a detail. The product therefore needs boundaries outside the model itself.02 / FIELD NOTESThree layers worth separatingThe conversation interface collects messages and presents replies. An application layer decides which information and tools the assistant can access. A model layer generates or classifies text. Keeping these responsibilities separate makes it easier to protect credentials, enforce permissions and replace a provider. A browser should call an application endpoint, not contain a private model API key. A public demonstration without that boundary is not a production architecture.03 / FIELD NOTESA useful example: a documentation assistantConsider a visitor asking whether a product supports exporting a report. The application retrieves a relevant, approved documentation passage and asks the model to answer from that context. The reply can link to the source and offer contact details if the documentation does not answer the question. This retrieval approach reduces guesswork; it does not eliminate errors. Old documents, conflicting policies and missing context still need handling.04 / FIELD NOTESWhen a rule-based flow is the better choiceFor a small set of predictable questions, buttons and deterministic replies may be clearer, cheaper and easier to verify than generative answers. A booking confirmation or a price calculation should follow validated rules. A hybrid system can use AI to understand the request while leaving important actions to explicit application logic. Never use a fluent answer as authorization to make a payment, change an account or disclose private information.05 / FIELD NOTESEvaluate before you launchWrite representative questions with expected answers and acceptable escalation behavior. Include unclear requests, out-of-scope questions, outdated content and attempts to obtain private information. Measure answer quality, source accuracy, latency and cost under realistic load. Define a human handoff and keep a way to disable the assistant. This article describes general architecture, not a claim that these features have all been implemented in an MBK project.NEXT / FROM READING TO PLANNINGChoose a scoped next step.Refer to OpenAI API documentation for current provider requirements. Check policies and documentation again before implementation.Explore the service scope ↗ · Find related resources ↗

/article-api-integration.html.main_text: Home/API Integration Checklist for Web Projectslesson / MBK GLOBALAPI Integration Checklist for Small Web ProjectsA successful API connection is more than a request that returns JSON once.IN THIS GUIDEProject overviewBakhtawar KhanFounder, MBK Global2 min read · Practical learning notesLearn. Apply. Make it your own.More learning resources ↗MBK JOURNAL / APIS / ENGINEERING← All articlesNEW APIS / ENGINEERINGPRACTICAL NOTES / BAKHTAWAR KHANRead the contract before writing codeBefore integrating an API, read its documentation and identify the required method, endpoint, authentication, request fields, response shape, rate limits and error codes. Confirm whether the provider permits browser-side requests and what its CORS policy allows.Design for failure, not only successful JSONTreat network responses as untrusted input. Handle timeouts, offline states, invalid JSON, rate limits and server errors. Validate required fields before using them in the interface, and show users a clear message when something fails rather than leaving a spinner running forever.Keep private credentials off the clientDo not put private API keys or long-lived secrets in browser JavaScript or public repositories. If a secret is required, use a server-side function or backend, apply least privilege and store the secret in environment variables. Avoid logging tokens or personal data.Test the handover as well as the requestTest the happy path and failure paths with sample inputs. Document any dependency on an external API, because availability, pricing and response formats can change.Further reading: Official documentation ↗BAKHTAWAR KHAN · APIS / ENGINEERINGDiscuss a related project ↗A small release checklist you can actually testWrite the expected behavior for each state before connecting the interface. For an empty result, show an honest empty state rather than an error. For a failed request, preserve the user’s input and offer a safe retry. For a 429 response, respect the provider’s retry guidance; repeatedly retrying immediately can make the limit worse.Contract: record the endpoint, method, required fields and authentication model from current provider documentation.Boundaries: reject missing or incorrectly typed fields before they reach display or calculation code.Cancellation: cancel obsolete requests when the user changes the query or leaves the view, and do not present cancellation as a server failure.Privacy: avoid putting tokens, customer information or full private responses in logs and screenshots.Handover: document rate limits, credentials ownership, provider costs and what happens when the upstream service is unavailable.What should be verified before release?Exercise a normal response, an empty response, invalid JSON, a missing required field, an authentication failure, a rate limit and a timeout. Check that the loading indicator stops in every path and that error text can be understood without opening developer tools. Test with keyboard navigation and a slow connection as well as a desktop connection.This checklist is general engineering guidance, not a claim that a particular provider integration has been built or certified by the author. For a React-specific companion, read designing interfaces around real API states. For a scoped implementation enquiry, review AI and API integration services.Reference: MDN: using the Fetch API.Back to the MBK journal ↗

/whatsapp-business-chatbot-guide.html.main_text: Home/WhatsApp Chatbots for Businesses: Features, Use Cases, and ImplementationField guide / BAKHTAWAR KHANWhatsApp Chatbots for Businesses: Features, Use Cases, and ImplementationPlan a supported WhatsApp enquiry flow with clear consent, human handoff and realistic provider dependencies.Explore the work ↗Start a conversation ↗Educational guide · By Bakhtawar Khan · General guidance, not a claim of personally tested provider integrations.01 / FIELD NOTESStart with one customer journeyA useful business chatbot might answer opening-hours questions, collect the category of an enquiry or route a support request. Define a narrow success condition before adding a model: for example, help a visitor reach the right person without repeating their issue. Draw the happy path and the places where a person must intervene. A long automated conversation is not necessarily a successful one.02 / FIELD NOTESA draft link is not a WhatsApp chatbotA click-to-chat link opens WhatsApp with a prepared message. It does not receive messages, deliver automated replies or maintain a support workflow. This portfolio’s project form prepares a WhatsApp draft; the visitor sends it themselves. An actual bot requires a supported Business Platform integration, authorized account access and infrastructure that can receive events and call the messaging API.03 / FIELD NOTESWhat platform approval changesBusiness onboarding, message templates, customer-service windows, pricing and account eligibility depend on current Meta rules and the chosen provider. Check the official documentation at the time of implementation rather than relying on a permanently fixed number of hours or a quoted fee in a blog post. Provider access and template approval should be explicit project dependencies, not hidden assumptions in a delivery promise.04 / FIELD NOTESMap the data before mapping the repliesFor a simple lead flow, a name, enquiry category and preferred callback time may be sufficient. Explain why the information is requested, where it goes and how a person can ask for deletion. Avoid collecting passwords, payment credentials or sensitive documents through a general-purpose chat. Restrict who can read conversation records and agree a retention period rather than keeping every message indefinitely.05 / FIELD NOTESImplement and test the failure pathsA webhook handler should verify requests, handle repeated delivery safely and respond quickly while longer work happens separately. Track provider message status without assuming that an accepted request means a person read it. Test invalid input, expired permissions, opt-outs and handoff when nobody is available. Keep a manual alternative and a rollback plan. These are educational implementation considerations; no account approval or live integration is claimed here.NEXT / FROM READING TO PLANNINGChoose a scoped next step.Refer to WhatsApp Business Platform documentation for current provider requirements. Check policies and documentation again before implementation.Explore the service scope ↗ · Find related resources ↗

Make it your own.More learning resources ↗MBK JOURNAL / ARTICLE← All articles01 PROFILEA PERSONAL INTRODUCTIONThe person behind the portfolioI’m Bakhtawar Khan, also known online as MBK. I’m interested in web development, practical AI tools, APIs, automation and the craft of making digital experiences feel clear and useful. /deployment-and-maintenance-guide.html.main_text: Home/Deploying and Maintaining a Static Websitelesson / MBK GLOBALDeploying and Maintaining a Static WebsiteA reliable deployment process makes the published output predictable and gives you a way to detect regressions before and after release.IN THIS GUIDE01Confirm the publish directory02Keep redirects direct03Set sensible response headers04Use a repeatable test checklist05Deploy with a rollback pathBakhtawar KhanFounder, MBK Global2 min read · Practical learning notesLearn. Apply. Make it your own.More learning resources ↗MBK Global · Practical guideConfirm the publish directoryIdentify which directory the host actually publishes and keep hosting configuration files such as Netlify _headers and _redirects in the appropriate publish root. Do not assume a configuration file for another provider controls the live deployment.Keep redirects directUse permanent redirects only when a URL has a close, useful replacement. Avoid loops, chains and redirecting unrelated pages to the homepage. Update internal links and sitemap entries to point directly to final canonical URLs.Set sensible response headersUse HTTPS, nosniff, a restrictive referrer policy and framing protection appropriate to the site. Begin Content Security Policy in report-only mode when existing inline code or third-party resources may be affected. Review reports before enforcement.Use a repeatable test checklistCheck HTML structure, internal links, metadata, canonical URLs, sitemap coverage, structured data, image references, keyboard navigation and responsive layouts. Record the command and result for each test rather than marking unrun checks as passed.Deploy with a rollback pathKeep an untouched source backup and a separate implementation copy. Review the diff, publish only after owner review, then test live status codes, redirects and headers. Keep Search Console and real-user performance monitoring as post-deployment tasks. /article-ai-automation.html.main_text: Home/AI automation workflow designlesson / MBK GLOBALPractical AI Automation: design the workflow before the promptReliable automation starts with a well-defined process, not just a clever prompt.IN THIS GUIDEProject overviewBakhtawar KhanFounder, MBK Global2 min read · Practical learning notesLearn. Apply. Make it your own.More learning resources ↗MBK JOURNAL / AI / AUTOMATION← All articlesNEW AI / AUTOMATIONPRACTICAL NOTES / BAKHTAWAR KHANDefine the workflow before choosing AIChoose one repetitive task and map its current steps. Define what triggers the workflow, which data it may access, what output is expected and how a person will know whether it worked. If the task is not clear enough to explain as a checklist, automation will probably make the confusion faster.Make review and escalation explicitStart with a narrow prototype using non-sensitive sample data. Set expectations for output format, validate required fields and handle missing or contradictory information. Plan for API failures, model uncertainty, retries and duplicate events. Keep credentials in secure server-side configuration.Protect inputs and evaluate failuresUse human review for consequential actions, external messages, financial decisions or changes that are hard to reverse. Add logs that help diagnose failures while minimizing personal data. A workflow should have a safe stop path and a way to undo or correct mistakes.Evaluate the workflow against a small set of realistic examples before expanding it. Record where it succeeds, where it fails and which cases require a person. Do not promise perfect accuracy or full autonomy.Further reading: Official documentation ↗BAKHTAWAR KHAN · AI / AUTOMATIONDiscuss a related project ↗Back to the MBK journal ↗

/article-react-performance.html.main_text: Home/React performance checklistlesson / MBK GLOBALReact Performance: a practical checklist before optimizingFast interfaces begin with measurement, not random code changes.IN THIS GUIDEProject overviewBakhtawar KhanFounder, MBK Global2 min read · Practical learning notesLearn. Apply. Make it your own.More learning resources ↗MBK JOURNAL / FRONTEND / PERFORMANCE← All articlesNEW FRONTEND / PERFORMANCEPRACTICAL NOTES / BAKHTAWAR KHANMeasure a specific slow interactionWhen a React interface feels slow, it is tempting to add memoization everywhere or rewrite large components. A better first step is to reproduce the problem and measure it. Identify whether the delay comes from JavaScript execution, network requests, large images, repeated rendering or layout shifts.Reduce work before adding memoizationStart with the user journey. Check the initial page load, the first meaningful interaction and the slowest route on a real mobile device. Use browser performance tools and Lighthouse as diagnostic aids, then verify findings instead of treating one score as the whole story.Keep network states usableKeep components focused, avoid unnecessary state duplication and split large bundles when the route or feature genuinely benefits. Optimize images, remove unused dependencies and provide loading, empty and error states. Use memoization only when profiling shows it helps; it can make code harder to maintain when used without a reason.Verify the result on a real deviceA useful before-and-after note should record the tested page, device or throttling profile, what changed and the measured result. Never claim a speed improvement without comparable measurements.Further reading: Official documentation ↗BAKHTAWAR KHAN · FRONTEND / PERFORMANCEDiscuss a related project ↗Back to the MBK journal ↗

/about.html.main_text: Home/Bakhtawar Khan founder of MBK GlobalTHE FOUNDER / A PERSONAL INTRODUCTIONBakhtawarKhan.Founder of MBK Global · Independent digital builderI’m Bakhtawar Khan, known online as Mr Bakhtawar and the founder of MBK Global. I build for the web—and for the people on the other side of the screen. /automation-and-ai-workflows-guide.html.main_text: Home/Automation and Responsible AI Workflowslesson / MBK GLOBALAutomation and Responsible AI WorkflowsAutomation is most useful when the task is well-defined, failure is detectable, and a person can review consequential outputs. AI can assist a workflow, but it should not remove accountability.IN THIS GUIDE01Map the task first02Validate inputs and outputs03Protect secrets and personal data04Design for failure and review05Monitor and document changesBakhtawar KhanFounder, MBK Global2 min read · Practical learning notesLearn. Apply. Make it your own.More learning resources ↗MBK Global · Practical guideMap the task firstDescribe the input, expected output, owner, success criteria and failure path before selecting tools. Automate repetitive, bounded work before tasks involving sensitive data or high-impact decisions.Validate inputs and outputsCheck required fields, data types, allowed ranges and external response shapes. Treat model-generated text and third-party API responses as untrusted until validated. Handle missing fields and service failures explicitly.Protect secrets and personal dataKeep API keys out of public source files and client-side JavaScript when they grant privileged access. Use environment secrets on the server or hosting platform, limit permissions and rotate exposed credentials. Send only the data a workflow needs.Design for failure and reviewPlan for timeouts, rate limits, retries, duplicate requests and partial completion. Log enough to diagnose problems without recording secrets. Require human approval for external actions that are difficult to reverse.Monitor and document changesRecord what the automation does, its dependencies, limitations and owner. Test edge cases after changes and provide a safe way to pause or roll back the workflow. Never describe an AI-assisted result as verified until it has actually been checked. About this guide: This is general educational guidance. Adapt recommendations to your site's actual stack, risk and audience, and verify changes before publishing. Explore related work: web development, projects, and contact.

/delivered-project.html.main_text: Home/Project Process & Deliverydirectory / MBK GLOBALClear steps.Thoughtful work.Final delivery.A good project should never feel like a mystery. I’m Bakhtawar Khan, founder of MBK Global. Here’s the practical path we follow to turn your idea into a considered, useful digital result—with clear communication, agreed milestones and a proper handover.MBK / PROJECT DELIVERY From “I have an idea” to “It’s ready.”Every project is different, so the exact deliverables and timeline are agreed before work begins. This four-step framework keeps expectations clear and gives you opportunities to review the direction along the way. First · DiscoverWe understand your idea.First, we discuss your goals, audience, references, features, deadline and budget. We identify the real problem to solve and define what success should look like.Project brief and requirementsGoals, audience and priorities01 02Second · PlanWe shape the direction.Next, we turn the brief into a practical plan. Depending on the project, this may include page structure, a visual direction, a feature list, milestones and a delivery schedule.Scope and milestones agreedDesign direction or technical plan Third · Build & reviewWe create, test and refine.Then the design or development work begins. You can review agreed checkpoints, share feedback and help us refine the details before final delivery.Build, integration and quality checksFeedback and agreed revisions03 04Finally · DeliverYour final project is handed over.Finally, we review the agreed deliverables and hand over the finished work. Depending on the scope, this can include source files, deployment assistance, documentation and guidance for what comes next.Final review against the briefHandover and next-step guidance THE FINISH LINE IS A HANDOVERBuilt with purpose.Delivered with clarity.Our goal is not just to finish a task, but to give you a result you understand and can move forward with. The final scope, payment stages, revisions, third-party fees and ongoing support are agreed in writing before work starts—so there are no hidden assumptions.Explore services ↗Start your project ↗Chat on WhatsApp ↗

/react-api-interface-design.html.main_text: WEB DEVELOPMENT / FIELD GUIDEDesigning React Interfaces Around Real API StatesA practical guide to loading, empty, error and stale-data states in API-connected React interfaces.Educational guidance by Bakhtawar Khan · Approximately 4 minutes to read01 / INTERFACE CRAFTStart with the request lifecycleA data-driven interface is not just a successful response rendered as a list. Before a request finishes, people need to know whether the application is working. When it finishes without results, they need a useful explanation. If it fails, they need a safe next step. Sketch these states before deciding how a component should look. This often exposes missing requirements earlier than building the polished success screen first.02 / INTERFACE CRAFTKeep the model explicitRepresent idle, loading, success and error deliberately rather than deriving every screen from whether an array happens to be empty. An empty array can mean no results, a request that has not run, or a failed request that silently fell back to an empty value. Separate these meanings. React state or an established data-fetching library can express the lifecycle; choose based on the application rather than adding a dependency for a single request.03 / INTERFACE CRAFTDesign the empty state around intentIf a search returns nothing, keep the query visible and offer a way to clear filters. If an account has no records yet, explain how to create the first one. These are different situations even though both contain zero items. Avoid suggesting that a user has done something wrong when the system simply has nothing to show. A short explanation and a relevant next action are usually enough.04 / INTERFACE CRAFTTreat failures as part of the interactionA timeout, permission failure and malformed response need different handling. Retry only when retrying is safe and likely to help. Keep a user’s unsent input intact. Never expose access tokens or raw provider responses in an error message. For important actions, prevent duplicate submissions while a request is pending and explain whether the outcome is unknown rather than telling the user to repeat an operation blindly.05 / INTERFACE CRAFTHandle requests that arrive out of orderWhen a user changes a filter quickly, an older response may arrive after the newest one. Ensure the earlier request cannot overwrite the currently selected view. Cancellation with AbortController or request identity checks can help, depending on the fetching approach. Clean up effects and check the current React documentation; do not rely on a demonstration that only works when every request returns in a predictable order.06 / INTERFACE CRAFTMake the result understandable to everyoneUse visible status text and an appropriate live region for meaningful updates without announcing every keystroke. Preserve sensible keyboard focus when results change. A loading indicator should not be the only information available, and motion should respect user preferences. Keep the layout stable with correctly sized images and predictable content regions, but avoid presenting placeholders as real records.07 / INTERFACE CRAFTTest the experience, not only the endpointUse controlled responses to test slow requests, empty datasets, permission errors and unexpected values. Check a small screen, keyboard navigation and repeated interactions. Confirm that links and form state survive recoverable errors. These checks describe a general development practice, not a claim that every linked MBK project implements every technique. Evaluate each project by its documented scope and current behavior.Continue with web development service scope, API integration notes and the official React learning guide. No affiliation is implied.

/content-strategy-and-search-intent.html.main_text: Home/Content Strategy and Search Intentlesson / MBK GLOBALContent Strategy and Search IntentA sustainable content strategy starts with real audience questions and the information you can reliably provide. Publishing fewer, more distinct pages is often more useful than scaling near-identical posts.IN THIS GUIDE01Build a topic inventory02Map intent to a page type03Create a useful brief04Write with evidence and clarity05Maintain and consolidate carefullyBakhtawar KhanFounder, MBK Global2 min read · Practical learning notesLearn. Apply. Make it your own.More learning resources ↗MBK Global · Practical guideBuild a topic inventoryList the pages you already have, their primary audience, purpose, supporting evidence and internal links. Identify overlap before drafting anything new. A page that serves a distinct task may deserve to remain separate even when it shares vocabulary with another page.Map intent to a page typePeople may want to learn a concept, compare options, complete a task or evaluate a service. Match the page format to that need: a checklist for implementation, a guide for learning, a project page for demonstrated work, and a contact page for enquiries.Create a useful briefState the intended reader, question, key points, facts that need verification, examples available, related internal pages and what the page should help the reader do next. Identify evidence gaps instead of filling them with assumptions.Write with evidence and clarityUse plain language, explain unfamiliar terms and provide concrete steps or examples. Separate verified experience from general advice. Do not invent client results, testimonials, qualifications, publication dates or statistics.Maintain and consolidate carefullyReview pages for accuracy, outdated links and overlap. If consolidating URLs, choose the closest relevant destination, transfer genuinely useful information, update internal links and test redirects. Review Search Console data before irreversible removals when available. About this guide: This is general educational guidance. Adapt recommendations to your site's actual stack, risk and audience, and verify changes before publishing. Explore related work: web development, projects, and contact.

/blog.html.main_text: Find your next ideaHome/Articles & Guideslibrary / MBK GLOBALStories from the MBK universe.A personal journal about the person behind the projects, the ideas behind each platform and the lessons that come from learning by building. These are editorial introductions, not claims of finished or commercial-scale products.THE JOURNAL / IDEAS, BUILDS & LESSONS11 ARTICLESPROFILE · PROJECTS · DIGITAL CRAFT 01 PROFILEA PERSONAL INTRODUCTIONBakhtawar Khan: learning, building and sharing in publicA digital portfolio is more than a list of links. It can be a record of curiosity, progress and the work still ahead.I’m Bakhtawar Khan, also known online as MBK. I’m interested in web development, practical AI tools, APIs, automation and the craft of making digital experiences feel clear and useful. My approach is to learn through small projects: plan a simple idea, build an interface, test how it behaves and keep improving it.This website brings my projects, writing, visual work and online profiles together in one place. It is a work in progress by design. I want it to show not only finished links, but also the process behind them: what I’m exploring, what I’ve learned and what I want to make better next.My focus is on steady progress rather than pretending to know everything. I value practical learning, honest descriptions and the kind of collaboration where a clear problem leads to a useful result.BAKHTAWAR KHAN / MBK · PERSONAL PROFILERead full article ↗ 02 BRANDTHE DIGITAL STUDIO IDEAMBK Global: a home for creative digital workA brand direction that brings web experiences, design thinking and technology experiments under one identity.MBK Global represents the broader digital side of my work: websites, online experiences, creative concepts and experiments with emerging tools. The intention is to keep the brand flexible enough to explore different ideas while keeping one consistent standard—clear communication and thoughtful execution.Good digital work is not only about adding effects or making a page look impressive. It should help people understand what is offered, find what they need and take the next step without friction. That means content hierarchy, accessibility, performance and responsive behaviour matter just as much as visual style.As the projects grow, MBK Global can serve as a shared home for selected work and experiments. The brand is evolving alongside my skills, and this journal will help document that process.Visit MBK Global ↗MBK GLOBAL · BRAND NOTESRead full article ↗ 03 MEDIACONTENT & DISCOVERYMBK TV: thinking about a digital media destinationA media concept where clarity, navigation and a strong editorial structure can make content easier to discover.MBK TV is one of the digital projects in the MBK collection. The idea behind a media platform is simple: visitors should be able to understand what the platform covers, discover relevant content and move between sections naturally.Media websites need more than a logo and a feed. They benefit from consistent categories, readable headlines, thoughtful page speed and metadata that describes each page accurately. If content is updated regularly, a sitemap and clear internal links also help search engines understand the site's structure.The project is an ongoing web experiment, and its exact features may change. I see it as a chance to explore how a digital media experience can balance visual identity with practical usability.Explore MBK TV ↗MBK TV · PROJECT STORYRead full article ↗ 04 DATA UIMAKING INFORMATION LEGIBLEMBK Markets: exploring a clearer view of market dataA market interface is a design challenge: show useful information without overwhelming the person reading it.MBK Markets explores the presentation of market-related information through a web interface. Financial data can be dense, and a useful interface needs a strong hierarchy: the most important values should be easy to scan, supporting details should be available when needed and the layout should remain usable on smaller screens.Charts and price figures also need context. Users should be able to identify what a number represents, the time period it covers and whether the data is current. Visual polish is valuable, but it should never imply that information is live or authoritative unless the underlying data source supports that claim.This project is a learning space for data presentation, responsive layout and the details that make information easier to understand. It is not financial advice.Explore MBK Markets ↗MBK MARKETS · INTERFACE NOTESRead full article ↗ 05 WEB TOOLSSMALL UTILITIES, REAL LESSONSMBK Downloader and Text to Handwriting: focused tools for focused tasksA useful tool should make one job feel straightforward, not turn a simple task into a complicated workflow.MBK Downloader and Text to Handwriting explore two different utility ideas. A downloader interface should explain what input is expected, present available options clearly and communicate errors without confusing the visitor. It also needs to respect the terms and rights that apply to the content being handled.A handwriting-style tool is a creative experience. Its value comes from giving typed text a more personal visual treatment while keeping the workflow simple: enter text, adjust the output and decide what to do next. Readability and export quality matter more than decorative complexity.Working on small utilities is a useful way to practice validation, interface states, responsive behaviour and API integration. It also reinforces an important product lesson: the best interface is often the one that removes unnecessary steps.MBK Downloader ↗ / Text to Handwriting ↗MBK UTILITIES · BUILD LOGRead full article ↗ 06 LEARNINGCONTENT WITH CARENoor-e-Quran: creating a calm digital learning experienceA faith-oriented website benefits from simplicity, respect and a clear path to the content visitors came to find.Noor-e-Quran is part of the MBK project collection. A website in this space should put the learning experience first: readable typography, comfortable spacing, thoughtful navigation and a calm visual style can help visitors focus on the content rather than the interface.Accuracy and trust are especially important for religious material. Sources should be clearly identified, content should be handled respectfully and any translations or explanatory text should be reviewed carefully. Accessibility on mobile devices also matters, because many visitors use a phone as their primary screen.The project is an opportunity to think about how design choices can support a meaningful subject without distracting from it.Visit Noor-e-Quran ↗NOOR-E-QURAN · PROJECT STORYRead full article ↗ 07 PROCESSTHE WORK NEVER REALLY STOPSWhat comes next for the MBK portfolioA professional portfolio grows through accurate details, regular maintenance and real evidence of work.The next stage is not simply to add more pages. It is to make every page more useful: keep project links working, add screenshots and case studies where available, explain the problem each project addresses and document the decisions made along the way.For the website itself, that means keeping navigation consistent, making images accessible, checking page speed, adding descriptive metadata and maintaining an accurate sitemap. For the writing, it means publishing real updates when there is something meaningful to share rather than filling the site with empty announcements.This portfolio should continue to reflect where I am today while leaving room for what I learn next. /personal-branding-and-online-identity.h.main_text: Home/Personal Branding and Online Identitylesson / MBK GLOBALPersonal Branding and Online IdentityA credible professional presence helps people understand who you are, what you work on and how they can verify or contact you. Consistency matters more than creating profiles on every platform.IN THIS GUIDE01Keep identity details consistent02Show work with context03Use evidence, not inflated claims04Make contact pathways clear05Maintain the profile over timeBakhtawar KhanFounder, MBK Global2 min read · Practical learning notesLearn. Apply. Make it your own.More learning resources ↗MBK Global · Practical guideKeep identity details consistentUse the same preferred name, role descriptions, brand name and canonical website across profiles where you actively participate. Keep a single source of truth for public links and update outdated references when the production host changes.Show work with contextFor each project, explain the problem, your contribution, technologies used and current status. Link to a working demo or repository only when it is genuinely available. Distinguish experiments and learning projects from paid client work.Use evidence, not inflated claimsDo not publish invented client names, testimonials, awards, metrics or qualifications. If you are still building experience, describe the actual skills and projects you can demonstrate and identify areas you are continuing to learn.Make contact pathways clearKeep contact, booking and social links current and test them periodically. Explain what information a form collects and avoid requesting sensitive details that are not necessary. Never publish private contact data without considering the consequences.Maintain the profile over timeReview your portfolio after meaningful project changes, remove broken links and keep descriptions factual. Create profiles only on services you intend to maintain; low-quality mass profile creation can damage trust rather than build it. About this guide: This is general educational guidance. Adapt recommendations to your site's actual stack, risk and audience, and verify changes before publishing. Explore related work: web development, projects, and contact.

This portfolio documents his interests, projects and ongoing learning.Learn more ↗ 009 PROJECTSWhat does MBK stand for on this website?MBK is the short personal brand used by Bakhtawar Khan across this portfolio and related digital projects.Learn more ↗ 010 PROJECTSWhat is MBK Global?MBK Global is the umbrella identity for digital projects, web experiences and technology experiments associated with Bakhtawar Khan. If a link appears outdated, contact the portfolio owner.Learn more ↗ 014 PROJECTSDoes this portfolio guarantee search rankings?No. SEO work can improve technical accessibility and content clarity, but search engines decide indexing and rankings. No specific position or timeline is guaranteed.Learn more ↗ 015 PROJECTSCan you help improve an existing website?Potentially. Share the website URL, goals, current problems and the changes you want. The recommended approach depends on the codebase and access available.Learn more ↗ 016 PROJECTSCan you create a personal portfolio website?A portfolio can be scoped around biography, projects, skills, contact information, accessibility and SEO. Design and features should match the person’s real experience and goals.Learn more ↗ 017 PROJECTSCan you build a business website?Business websites can include service pages, contact forms, location details, FAQs and relevant conversion paths. Requirements should be agreed before implementation.Learn more ↗ 018 PROJECTSCan you build an online store?An online store requires product data, checkout, payment-provider support, shipping rules, policies and security considerations. Feasibility depends on platform and scope.Learn more ↗ 019 PROJECTSCan a website include appointment booking?Yes, if a suitable booking service or custom workflow is selected. Calendar rules, notifications, time zones and customer data handling should be defined first.Learn more ↗ 020 PROJECTSCan you add a training academy to a website?An academy may need course pages, enrolment, learner accounts, progress tracking and payments. The exact feature set should be planned around the learning model.Learn more ↗ 021 PROJECTSCan you integrate third-party APIs?API integration can connect a website to an external service when valid credentials, documentation, permissions and acceptable usage limits are available.Learn more ↗ 022 PROJECTSWhat information is needed for an API project?Share the API documentation, desired user flow, authentication method, expected traffic, error cases and whether any sensitive data is involved. Never send passwords or secret keys in public messages.Learn more ↗ 023 PROJECTSCan you build an AI-powered feature?AI features can be explored when the task, input data, expected output, evaluation criteria and budget for API usage are clear.Learn more ↗ 024 PROJECTSCan you automate repetitive work?Automation may connect forms, spreadsheets, notifications and business tools. First map the current steps, exceptions, permissions and what should happen when a step fails.Learn more ↗ 025 PROJECTSCan you build a WhatsApp bot?A WhatsApp automation project depends on the chosen provider, approved APIs, messaging policies, user consent and the intended conversation flow.Learn more ↗ 026 PROJECTSWhat is technical SEO?Technical SEO focuses on making a site easier for search engines to crawl and understand, including indexability, canonical URLs, metadata, structured data, internal links and sitemaps.Learn more ↗ 027 PROJECTSDo meta keywords improve Google rankings?Google Search does not use the meta keywords tag for web ranking. Clear page content, titles, links and technical accessibility are more useful priorities.Learn more ↗ 028 SERVICESHow should page titles be written?Use a unique, concise title that accurately describes the page and naturally includes the main topic or entity. Avoid repetitive keyword stuffing.Learn more ↗ 029 SERVICESWhat makes a good meta description?A helpful description summarises the actual page in natural language and gives searchers a clear reason to visit. Search engines may choose a different snippet.Learn more ↗ 030 SERVICESWhat is a canonical URL?A canonical URL signals the preferred version of similar or duplicate pages. It should point to the correct live URL and be consistent with internal links and sitemaps.Learn more ↗ 031 SERVICESWhat is an XML sitemap?An XML sitemap lists canonical URLs that a site owner wants search engines to discover. It does not guarantee indexing.Learn more ↗ 032 SERVICESWhat does robots.txt do?The robots.txt file gives crawlers instructions about crawling paths. It is not a reliable way to keep private information out of search results.Learn more ↗ 033 SERVICESHow can I check whether a page is indexed?Use Google Search Console URL Inspection for the exact live URL. A page being crawlable does not automatically mean it will be indexed.Learn more ↗ 034 SERVICESWhy might Google show the wrong snippet?Google may generate snippets from page text or choose a different title based on the query. Keep visible content, title tags and metadata accurate and consistent.Learn more ↗ 035 SERVICESWhy might a page not appear for my full name?Search visibility depends on competition, relevance, indexing, links and how clearly the site identifies the person. Ranking changes are not immediate or guaranteed.Learn more ↗ 036 SERVICESShould every page link to every other page?No. Link pages where the destination is genuinely useful. A clear navigation menu and contextual links are better than repeating the same links excessively.Learn more ↗ 037 SERVICESHow many FAQs should a website have?Add questions that real visitors need answered. A large FAQ can help users when it stays accurate and organised, but volume alone does not improve rankings.Learn more ↗ 038 SERVICESShould FAQ structured data be added?Structured data must match visible page content and follow current search-engine policies. Valid markup does not guarantee a rich result.Learn more ↗ 039 SERVICESWhat is image SEO?Image SEO includes descriptive filenames, useful alt text, appropriate formats, responsive sizing, compression and placing images near relevant content.Learn more ↗ 040 SERVICESHow should alt text be written?Describe the meaningful information conveyed by the image in context. Avoid stuffing names and keywords or repeating nearby captions unnecessarily.Learn more ↗ 041 SERVICESShould decorative images have alt text?Purely decorative images should generally use an empty alt attribute so assistive technology can skip them.Learn more ↗ 042 SERVICESCan images help people find my profile?Well-labelled, relevant images can improve accessibility and image discovery, but search visibility depends on many factors and cannot be promised.Learn more ↗ 043 SERVICESWhat is structured data?Structured data is machine-readable markup that describes page entities or content. It must be accurate, visible where required and consistent with the page.Learn more ↗ 044 SERVICESWhat is the difference between SEO and AEO?SEO helps content be discovered in search engines. AEO is a broad term for structuring useful answers clearly for answer-oriented search experiences; neither guarantees placement.Learn more ↗ 045 SERVICESWhat does GEO mean in digital content?GEO is often used to describe making information clear and citable in generative search experiences. Strong factual content and clear entity information are sensible foundations, not a guarantee.Learn more ↗ 046 SERVICESCan you help with website accessibility?Accessibility improvements can include semantic headings, keyboard navigation, visible focus, sufficient contrast, meaningful labels and descriptive link text.Learn more ↗ 047 SERVICESWhy is mobile responsiveness important?Responsive layouts help content and controls work across different screen sizes and support a more usable experience on phones and tablets.Learn more ↗ 048 SERVICESHow can a website load faster?Common improvements include compressing images, reducing unnecessary scripts, caching assets, limiting heavy third-party code and measuring real performance.Learn more ↗ 049 SERVICESDo you use a particular framework?The portfolio demonstrates work across web technologies such as HTML, CSS, JavaScript and React. The best stack depends on project requirements and maintenance needs.Learn more ↗ 050 SERVICESCan you work with existing HTML and CSS?Yes, improvements can be planned around existing code after reviewing its structure, dependencies, visual design and deployment process.Learn more ↗ 051 SERVICESCan you help with React projects?React work can include components, page layouts, state handling, accessibility, performance and API integration, depending on the existing project.Learn more ↗ 052 SERVICESCan you help debug a website?Share a reproducible issue, browser or device details, relevant error messages and the expected behaviour. Remove secrets and personal data before sharing logs.Learn more ↗ 053 SERVICESCan you review website security?A scoped review may cover common web risks and safer implementation practices. A proper security assessment needs explicit authorisation and a clearly agreed scope.Learn more ↗ 054 SERVICESWhat is responsible reverse engineering?Reverse engineering can be used to understand software behaviour where legally authorised. Work must respect applicable law, licences, privacy and system-owner permissions.Learn more ↗ 055 SERVICESCan you test a website I do not own?Only with explicit permission from the owner. Testing should stay within an agreed scope and must not disrupt services or access data without authorisation.Learn more ↗ 056 SERVICESHow should API keys be protected?Keep secrets on the server or in a secure environment manager, rotate exposed keys, apply least-privilege permissions and never commit credentials to public repositories.Learn more ↗ 057 SERVICESWhat is HTTPS?HTTPS encrypts data exchanged between a browser and a website and helps verify the site’s server identity. It does not by itself make every site feature secure.Learn more ↗ 058 PROCESSDo you provide cloud or VPS setup?Cloud and VPS tasks can be discussed around operating system, access controls, backups, updates, monitoring and budget. Exact requirements determine the approach.Learn more ↗ 059 PROCESSWhat is the difference between VPS and shared hosting?A VPS generally provides a more isolated virtual server environment, while shared hosting places multiple sites in a managed environment. The right choice depends on needs and administration skills.Learn more ↗ 060 PROCESSCan you help with domain setup?Domain configuration can involve DNS records, hosting targets, redirects and email records. Changes should be verified carefully to avoid interrupting existing services.Learn more ↗ 061 PROCESSCan you deploy a website on Vercel?Static and supported web applications can be deployed on Vercel when build settings, environment variables and project configuration are correct.Learn more ↗ 062 PROCESSCan you help with GitHub?GitHub workflows may include repository organisation, commits, branches, pull requests, deployment connections and troubleshooting build failures.Learn more ↗ 063 PROCESSWhat should a project brief include?Include the problem, target audience, key pages, required features, examples, content availability, budget range, timeline and who will approve the work.Learn more ↗ 064 PROCESSHow are project timelines decided?Timelines depend on complexity, content readiness, integrations, review cycles and third-party services. A realistic schedule should be agreed after scope is understood.Learn more ↗ 065 PROCESSDo you offer revisions?Revision rounds and what counts as a revision should be agreed before work starts so expectations remain clear.Learn more ↗ 066 PROCESSCan I request changes after launch?Post-launch changes can be scoped separately. Keep a list of issues, priorities and desired outcomes to make follow-up work efficient.Learn more ↗ 067 PROCESSWho provides website text and images?Responsibilities for copy, brand assets, photography and licensing should be agreed at the start. Any supplied assets should be cleared for use.Learn more ↗ 068 PROCESSCan you use my existing logo?An existing logo can usually be incorporated if you have the rights to use it and provide a suitable file format.Learn more ↗ 069 PROCESSCan you help with branding?Digital branding may include visual consistency, messaging, typography, colours and profile presentation, based on the existing identity and project goals.Learn more ↗ 070 PROCESSCan you create social profile links?A profile page can link to verified social accounts. Only accounts that belong to the person or brand should be represented as official.Learn more ↗ 071 PROCESSWhere can I find Bakhtawar Khan online?You can visit the About.me profile at about.me/muhammadbakhtawar and the Linktree page at linktr.ee/bakhtawark085, alongside the verified profiles listed on this site.Learn more ↗ 072 PROCESSWhat is the About.me profile for?The About.me page provides another public profile destination for Bakhtawar Khan. Keep its biography and links consistent with the main portfolio.Learn more ↗ 073 PROCESSWhat is the Linktree page for?The Linktree page can collect selected profile and project links in one place. Check that each destination is current and correctly labelled.Learn more ↗ 074 PROCESSWhat is MBK TV?MBK TV is one of the digital projects associated with the MBK portfolio. Visit its live site for current features and availability.Learn more ↗ 075 PROCESSWhat is MBK Markets?MBK Markets is a project exploring a market-data interface. It should not be treated as financial advice or a promise of investment performance.Learn more ↗ 076 PROCESSWhat is MBK Downloader?MBK Downloader is listed among the portfolio’s web-tool projects. Use services lawfully and respect copyright, platform terms and privacy.Learn more ↗ 077 PROCESSWhat is Noor-e-Quran by MBK?Noor-e-Quran is a faith-related digital project associated with the portfolio. Users should verify religious quotations and references against trusted sources.Learn more ↗ 078 PROCESSWhat is Text to Handwriting?Text to Handwriting is a tool concept that presents typed text in a handwriting-like style. Output quality and available features depend on the current live version.Learn more ↗ 079 PROCESSAre all projects production-ready?Not necessarily. Some entries may be experiments or works in progress. Check each project’s live page for its current state and capabilities.Learn more ↗ 080 PROCESSCan you collaborate with another developer?Collaboration can be discussed when responsibilities, communication, ownership, review process and deadlines are clear.Learn more ↗ 081 PROCESSCan you work with international clients?Remote collaboration may be possible. Time zones, payment arrangements, scope, communication and legal requirements should be discussed before commitment.Learn more ↗ 082 PROCESSWhat languages can project content use?Language requirements should be specified early. Multilingual websites may need translated content, language navigation and appropriate page metadata.Learn more ↗ 083 PROJECTSCan you make a website bilingual?A bilingual website can be planned with translated content, clear language switching and appropriate URL and metadata strategies for each language.Learn more ↗ 084 PROJECTSHow should contact forms handle personal data?Collect only necessary information, explain how it will be used, protect submissions and provide an appropriate privacy notice.Learn more ↗ 085 PROJECTSCan you add analytics?Analytics can be considered when the measurement goals, privacy obligations and consent requirements are understood. Avoid collecting unnecessary personal information.Learn more ↗ 086 PROJECTSWhat is a privacy policy?A privacy policy explains what personal information is collected, why it is processed, how it is stored or shared and what choices people have.Learn more ↗ 087 PROJECTSCan you add a cookie banner?A consent interface may be needed depending on the technologies used and applicable laws. It should reflect actual tracking behaviour rather than be purely decorative.Learn more ↗ 088 PROJECTSHow should website testimonials be used?Publish testimonials only with permission and ensure they reflect real feedback. Do not invent reviewers, identities, ratings or customer experiences.Learn more ↗ 089 PROJECTSCan I leave feedback on a project?Feedback can be shared through the contact page. Please identify the relevant project and describe what worked well or what should improve.Learn more ↗ 090 PROJECTSWhat does human rights mean online?Digital human rights include privacy, freedom of expression, access to information, non-discrimination and safety, subject to applicable law and the rights of others.Learn more ↗ 091 PROJECTSHow can websites respect human rights?Use privacy-conscious design, accessible content, clear policies, secure handling of data and respectful moderation. Avoid deceptive patterns and discriminatory treatment.Learn more ↗ 092 PROJECTSWhy is digital privacy important?Personal information can reveal sensitive details. Collecting less data, limiting access and explaining data use help reduce unnecessary privacy risks.Learn more ↗ 093 PROJECTSWhat is responsible AI use?Responsible AI use involves checking outputs, protecting sensitive data, being transparent about limitations and considering bias, safety and human oversight.Learn more ↗ 094 PROJECTSHow can a website be more inclusive?Use accessible markup, readable language, keyboard support, sufficient contrast, responsive layouts and respectful content that does not exclude groups of users.Learn more ↗ 095 PROJECTSHow do you handle project confidentiality?Discuss confidentiality needs before sharing sensitive information. Do not send passwords, private keys, identity documents or confidential customer data through public channels.Learn more ↗ 096 PROJECTSWhat happens if a third-party API changes?External APIs can change or become unavailable. Robust projects should handle errors, document dependencies and plan for maintenance when necessary.Learn more ↗ 097 PROJECTSHow do you test a website before launch?Testing can include mobile and desktop layouts, links, forms, keyboard use, accessibility basics, performance, metadata, redirects and key user journeys.Learn more ↗ 098 PROJECTSWhat should be checked after a site launches?Verify the live domain, HTTPS, redirects, page rendering, analytics if used, sitemap, robots rules, forms and Search Console status.Learn more ↗ 099 PROJECTSCan you guarantee a website will never go down?No. Hosting providers, networks, code and third-party services can fail. Monitoring, backups and recovery planning can reduce risk but not eliminate it.Learn more ↗ 100 PROJECTSHow often should website content be updated?Update content when facts, services, project links or policies change. Accuracy and usefulness matter more than publishing on an arbitrary schedule.Learn more ↗ 101 PROJECTSHow do I report a broken link?Send the page URL, the broken destination and what you expected to find through the contact page.Learn more ↗ 102 PROJECTSHow can I contact Bakhtawar Khan?Use the contact page or project enquiry form. Include a short description, relevant links and the best way to respond.Learn more ↗ 103 PROJECTSWhat should I include in a first message?Explain who you are, what you want to achieve, the current situation, important constraints and any deadline. Avoid sending credentials or sensitive personal data.Learn more ↗ 104 PROJECTSHow do I know if a project is a good fit?A good fit has a clearly described problem, realistic scope, available inputs, agreed responsibilities and a shared understanding of budget and timing.Learn more ↗ 105 PROJECTSDo you promise a specific result?No result should be promised before requirements and constraints are understood. Search rankings, traffic, conversion rates and third-party uptime are outside any single developer’s full control.Learn more ↗ 106 PROJECTSHow can I keep learning web development?Build small projects, read official documentation, test your assumptions, review errors and improve one part of a project at a time.Learn more ↗ 107 PROJECTSHow can I contribute to an open-source project?Read the project’s licence and contribution guide, reproduce an issue, make a focused change and explain what you tested.Learn more ↗ No matching questions yet.Try another keyword or switch back to all topics.Show all questions YOUR IDEA, NEXTStill have a question?Share a little context and get the conversation started.Send an enquiry ↗ MBK Global identity: Founder profile · Official links & projects · MBK Global website ↗

/telegram-bot-workflow-guide.html.main_text: Home/Telegram Bot Development: From Basic Commands to Automated WorkflowsField guide / BAKHTAWAR KHANTelegram Bot Development: From Basic Commands to Automated WorkflowsUnderstand commands, update delivery, permissions and reliable integrations before building a Telegram workflow.Explore the work ↗Start a conversation ↗Educational guide · By Bakhtawar Khan · General guidance, not a claim of personally tested provider integrations.01 / FIELD NOTESDefine the smallest useful command setStart with /start and /help, then one command that solves a specific task. A status bot might let an authorized user request a project update; a notification bot might let someone subscribe to a particular alert. Explain what the bot can do and how to stop notifications. Clear commands and visible choices are often more useful than a conversation that tries to interpret everything.02 / FIELD NOTESUpdates, webhooks and pollingTelegram sends bot activity as updates. An application can retrieve them by polling or receive them through a configured webhook, depending on the chosen deployment model. Plan how updates are acknowledged, retried and processed; do not treat delivery as exactly once. Use Telegram’s current documentation for webhook configuration and permitted connection details rather than copying assumptions from an old tutorial.03 / FIELD NOTESConnect external systems carefullySuppose a bot retrieves a ticket status from another service. Validate the request, check that the user is allowed to see the ticket, call the external API through a server-side integration and return a limited response. A Telegram user identifier is not automatically an account in that other service. Establish a deliberate linking or authorization step before exposing private data. Never accept an arbitrary URL and fetch it without destination controls.04 / FIELD NOTESTokens and group permissionsA bot token is a credential and must not be committed to source code, embedded in browser JavaScript or included in diagnostic screenshots. Rotate exposed tokens through the provider. Group privacy settings and permissions affect which messages and actions are available; a bot cannot assume access to all conversations. Ask for the minimum permissions needed and document who controls the bot account.05 / FIELD NOTESMake automation observable and reversibleKeep enough operational information to understand failed actions without logging unnecessary personal content. Limit repeated requests, handle upstream timeouts and avoid sending duplicate notifications when a job is retried. Test /help, invalid commands, permission failures and unsubscribe behavior. Give the account owner deployment notes and a stop procedure. This is a general planning guide, not evidence of a personally deployed Telegram service.NEXT / FROM READING TO PLANNINGChoose a scoped next step.Refer to Telegram Bot API documentation for current provider requirements. Check policies and documentation again before implementation.Explore the service scope ↗ · Find related resources ↗

/muhammad-bakhtawar-khan-digital-portfol.main_text: Home/Bakhtawar Khan digital portfoliolesson / MBK GLOBALBakhtawar Khan (MBK): A Digital Portfolio Built Around Practical ProjectsA guide to the personal portfolio of Bakhtawar Khan (MBK), founder of MBK Global, and how its projects, services and official links are organized.IN THIS GUIDEProject overviewBakhtawar KhanFounder, MBK Global2 min read · Practical learning notesLearn. Apply. Make it your own.More learning resources ↗MBK NOTES · SEO / AEO / GEOThe portfolio of Bakhtawar Khan (MBK) brings together selected web projects, digital technology interests, service areas and contact options. The goal is to make the person, the associated MBK Global brand and individual projects easier for visitors to distinguish. A useful portfolio should explain what exists, link to working examples and keep claims proportional to evidence. Explore the Founder Profile, Projects and Official Links.About the author: Bakhtawar Khan (MBK) is the founder of MBK Global. His stated focus areas include web development, AI/API integration, cybersecurity learning, technical SEO and digital branding.Read the MBK Founder Profile ↗ · MBK Global ↗ · Discuss a project ↗Published by Bakhtawar Khan · MBK Global. Content is educational and does not guarantee search rankings, security outcomes or AI citations.Personal perspective, learning and working principlesA PERSONAL PERSPECTIVEMy work begins with curiosity: how does this system work, who is it for, and what would make it more useful?01 / BACKGROUNDA growing practice.An independent point of view.I’m a technology enthusiast and digital creator building my skills across web development, modern JavaScript, React, applications, APIs and automation. I enjoy the point where technical problem-solving meets creative thinking: turning a complicated task into something understandable, usable and considered.This portfolio brings together my independent projects, experiments and professional interests. Some ideas become useful browser tools; others become a way to understand a new integration, a design decision or the behavior of an application. I want the work to communicate what I am learning—not suggest that the learning is finished.MBK is my professional identity. MBK Global is the associated brand connecting these projects and my longer-term direction. The person behind both is Bakhtawar Khan.The vision behind MBK Global ↗02 / TECHNICAL INTERESTSDifferent disciplines.The same curiosity.Web experiencesHTML, CSS, JavaScript and React provide a foundation for exploring responsive interfaces, reusable components, accessible navigation and clear application states. I care about how a product feels to use as well as how it is put together.Connected systemsAPIs interest me because they make separate tools work together. I’m learning through request handling, data transformation, integration experiments and understanding what happens when a service is slow, unavailable or returns unexpected data.AI & useful automationMy interests include knowledge-based assistants, chatbots, WhatsApp workflows and practical AI-powered tools. The useful question is not whether a task can be automated, but which parts should be—and where a person should remain in control.Beneath the interfaceReverse engineering, code analysis, technical research and web security help me investigate software behavior. My approach is permission-based and defensive: understand the system, respect its boundaries and protect other people’s information.Discoverability & qualityTechnical SEO, metadata, crawlability, page performance and thoughtful content structure connect development with the people who need the result. Good presentation should support useful information, not replace it.03 / LEARNING IN PRACTICEA more honest way to describe the toolkit.Visible in this portfolioHTML, CSS, JavaScript, React components, responsive layouts and structured technical content. The pages and linked projects are the places to review the work.Developing through experimentsPython, API integration, AI-assisted applications, conversational interfaces, workflow automation, performance and technical SEO.Exploring furtherBackend development, API design, databases, application architecture, Android and mobile applications, Telegram bots, supported social integrations, deployment and cloud tools.These distinctions matter. An interest is not a certification, and a prototype is not evidence of a production deployment. I prefer to explain a project’s actual scope and constraints rather than present every technology as an established specialization.04 / MAKING & REFLECTINGLearning becomes clearerwhen something has to work.Personal projects give me room to test an idea from more than one angle. MBK TV explores media discovery; MBK Markets explores a market-data interface; MBK Video Downloader and Text to Handwriting explore practical web utilities; Noor-e-Quran brings a different set of content and usability questions.Their value is not only in the visible result. Planning a flow, investigating a failure, checking a layout on a smaller screen and revisiting a confusing decision all develop a better understanding of the product. Features and availability can change; project pages provide the context rather than a promise of permanent functionality.Review the project collection ↗05 / WORKING PRINCIPLESClarity over complication.I start by understanding the need, the audience and the constraints. Then I break the problem into manageable pieces, build a small version, inspect what happens and refine it. I value reliable behavior, clear communication and room for feedback more than adding features simply because they are possible.Responsible technology is part of that process. Privacy, accessibility, respectful communication and permission-based research should shape the work from the beginning. Collecting less data, explaining limitations and making an interface usable for more people are practical development decisions—not finishing touches.06 / LOOKING AHEADDeeper understanding.More useful things.I want to strengthen my development skills, understand application architecture more deeply and connect AI, APIs and automation in ways that solve real problems. My direction includes useful tools, chatbots and digital products with clear purposes and understandable boundaries.My journey is still evolving. The aim is a stronger body of work and a professional identity grounded in thoughtful execution, not the size of the claims. If you have a project that fits that approach, I’d welcome a clear conversation about what you want to build.Discuss a project ↗Explore my reference library ↗Find official profiles ↗
